title: Throughput ledger and pairwise comparison UI with anomaly triage workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a searchable, auditable "throughput ledger" that stores run-level and slice-level performance metrics (tokens/sec, p95 latency, p50, error rates) and a lightweight pairwise comparison UI for front-line engineers/PMs to rapidly assess regressions. Complement this with an anomaly triage workflow that can (1) surface probable regressions, (2) attach likely culprits (CI commit/PR metadata), and (3) provide an actionable runbook for the oncall/owner to follow.

Why: Current benchmark artifacts are fragmented across ad-hoc logs and CSVs; triage requires manual aggregation and repeated runs. We need a single source-of-truth for performance history with fast diffs, deterministic drilldowns, and a repeatable triage flow to reduce mean-time-to-detect-and-fix regressions in serving runtime and model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger stores per-run metrics including tokens_per_sec, p95_ms, p50_ms, total_tokens, error_rate, model_name, model_version, commit_hash, seq_len_bucket, and batch_config for >= 90% of benchmark runs
UI: Pairwise compare view shows baseline vs candidate with delta, percent-change, and statistical significance indicator (bootstrap/confidence band) for tokens/sec and p95
Slice heatmap: p95 and tokens/sec heatmap across sequence-length buckets and model variants in the compare UI
Automatic anomaly flagging: system flags run as REGRESSION when p95 increases by >10% AND z-score > 2 compared to 30-day rolling baseline
CI metadata linking: each flagged run shows linked commit/PR and a list of changed files (when available)
Triage workflow: flag creates pre-filled triage ticket template (title/body) and posts a summary to #bench-triage Slack channel
Runbook: triage playbook link included in UI and ticket; actions include re-run with controlled seeds, isolate model vs infra (e.g., quantized vs fp16), and revert-to-last-known-good
Performance: ledger query latency for last-30-days rollup < 600ms for common queries (model+seqlen slice queries)
Tests: end-to-end test that injects synthetic regression signals into a synthetic run and verifies alerting + ticket generation
tasks: Design schema for ledger (primary keys, tags): model_name, model_version, commit_hash, run_id, seq_len_bucket, batch_config, metrics
Implement ingestion pipeline: canonicalize run metadata from CI, worker telemetry, and bench harness into ledger write path
Short-term store: ClickHouse/Timescale ingestion for fast queries and slices; long-term archive in S3 as partitioned Parquet
Implement regression detector service: compute rolling baselines, z-score, bootstrap confidence for p95 and tokens/sec
Backend API endpoints for pairwise compare and heatmap endpoints
Frontend: pairwise comparison page + heatmap overlay + delta table + commit links
CI integration: attach run_id and commit_hash in e2e bench runs; surface PR link when available
Alerting: wire anomaly detector to PagerDuty/Slack with adaptive thresholds per-model
Triage automation: generate pre-populated Linear ticket + add triage checklist and links to artifacts
Documentation: triage playbook, SLO impact matrix, and runbook for owners
technical_notes: Metric keys: use explicit typed keys to avoid schema drift (tokens_per_sec:float, p95_ms:float, p50_ms:float, error_rate:float)
Sequence-length bucketing: [<=64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024] to balance cardinality and signal fidelity
Delta fingerprint: compute a deterministic fingerprint per run (model+weights-hash+commit_hash+config) for fast grouping
Stat test: prefer bootstrap CI for small-sample p95 comparisons; fallback to z-score for large N; store sample histograms when available
Privacy: sample outputs hashed (sha256) when storing examples to enable regression repro without exposing PII
Storage: keep 90 days of high-resolution timeseries in ClickHouse, roll to S3 Parquet daily for retention beyond 90 days
Query patterns: optimize for pairwise comparison queries (baseline run id + candidate run id), and slice aggregations by seq_len_bucket and model_version
Failure modes: handle flaky runs by detecting multi-modal token/sec distributions across repeated runs; mark runs as FLAKY and exclude from baseline until stabilized
Cost control: sample full detailed traces on 1-in-20 runs and use aggregated metrics for every run to limit storage growth
